subject: Calibration plan: streaming latency & throughput benchmark
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@finserve.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: priya@finserve.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's perf discovery call

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — helpful session. To make sure we're aligned before your team runs the qualification:

- Target SLOs: P95 <= 120ms for single-request generations (typical 128-token prompts). We also want P99 <= 350ms for critical paths. These are what we currently promise in-prod for synchronous calls.
- Streaming: many of our flows use server-sent-chunked streaming; we care about first-byte latency and steady-state per-chunk latency (we'd like first-byte < 60ms).
- Throughput profile: baseline burst of ~80 req/s, expected sustained 35 req/s, but periodic spikes to 250 concurrent connections during market open (7–10 minutes).
- Concurrency: we need guidance on how concurrency relates to GPU slotting in your Dedicated offering; what metrics will you capture?

I'll attach a small sample of our prompt variants (sanitized) and a CSV of request mix. Also attaching a trace from last week's run for reference. Please confirm if the example artifacts are sufficient and what additional metadata you need for reproducibility.

Jordan
Head of Platform Engineering
FinServe Labs

Attachments: finserve_prompt_set_v2.csv (sanitized), example_trace_20261115.jsonl (request timing samples)
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan@finserve.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's perf discovery call

Jordan — great notes, and the artifacts you sent are exactly the type of inputs we need. Quick recap and what we plan to deliver for the qualification run: 

1) Measurements we'll produce (definitions):
  - First-byte latency: time from HTTP request received to first token emitted (measured at agent ingress). Reported p50/p95/p99.
  - Steady-state chunk latency: per-chunk generation latency once stream is active (p50/p95).
  - End-to-end completion latency: time to final token (p50/p95/p99), includes internal batching effects.
  - Throughput and concurrency maps: request-rate vs observed latency heatmap, and concurrency bucketed by active connections.
  - GPU-level utilization and queue depth traces correlated with request timestamps.

2) Reproducibility controls we want from you (small checklist):
  - Confirm prompt set and the ratio for each prompt class (you sent this in CSV — thanks).
  - Provide a deterministic random seed policy if your prompts include sampling variations.
  - Indicate any external tool calls (DB lookups) we should stub out; we will stub to avoid network variance.

3) Proposed harness artifacts we will share:
  - harness_config_v1.yaml (exec parameters: concurrency waveform, inter-arrival distribution, model variant pinned)
  - measurement-spec.md (naming and derivation rules for each metric)
  - example_trace_20261115.jsonl (we'll use your trace to seed arrival rates)

4) Open questions for you:
  - For the market-open spike, do those 250 concurrent connections map to 250 simultaneous in-flight token streams or 250 client sockets where many are idle? This changes batching behavior.
  - Is your P99 budget absolute at 350ms (hard SLA) or an ops target we can model as a SLO?

Next steps / timeline:
  - Today (Thu): we confirm the CSV + seed policy.
  - Fri: Redwood will push harness_config_v1.yaml and measurement-spec.md to the shared Drive.
  - Mon: run an initial calibration window (30m) using your trace-based arrival pattern; deliver initial heatmaps and latency distributions.

I've attached the harness_config_v1.yaml draft for your review; see the attachments listed.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, Jordan Lee <jordan@finserve.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Calibration plan: streaming latency & throughput benchmark

Jordan / Tessa — small clarifications and the exact measurement derivations we'll use for reporting (so nothing is ambiguous):

Measurement derivations (formal):
- first_byte_latency_ms = timestamp(first_token_emitted) - timestamp(request_received)
- chunk_latency_ms = timestamp(last_byte_of_chunk) - timestamp(first_byte_of_chunk) (bucketed per chunk index)
- completion_latency_ms = timestamp(final_token_emitted) - timestamp(request_received)
- p50/p95/p99 computed over non-error successful requests; errors are reported separately with error-rate by type.

Batching and concurrency notes:
- Our runtime uses a time-windowed continuous batching algorithm. For streams with long-lived KV caches we may reuse KV state across requests within the same session; we'll surface a flag in the report if KV hits materially affect latency.
- For your spike pattern: if 250 in-flight token streams are expected, we'll run a calibration that treats them as active low-rate streaming sessions (to reproduce backpressure). If instead 250 sockets with brief bursts, we will model them as short TTL requests to stress concurrency. Please confirm which of the two maps to your traffic.

Artifacts attached: harness_config_v1.yaml (contains waveforms and seed settings), small example of how we'll map your CSV ratios into the harness. We'll also include a mapping table of model variant -> quantization profile used during the run.

Action items assigned:
- Jordan: confirm "250 concurrent" semantics and seed policy (by EOD Fri).
- Jordan: confirm whether P99=350ms is hard SLA or target (by EOD Fri).
- Tessa: run calibration Mon AM and circulate initial heatmaps to the thread.
- Ben: prepare GPU utilization dashboard access for Jordan (temporary viewer account).

Kim
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan@finserve.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: priya@finserve.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Calibration plan: streaming latency & throughput benchmark

Thanks — confirming two points:

1) "250 concurrent" = 250 active in-flight token streams (many clients maintain long-lived streams during market open). Think of them as low-bandwidth but continuously-active sessions. Please model as active streams.
2) P99=350ms is a hard internal SLA for our synchronous critical path (we need to know margin at the 99th to decide on Dedicated commit sizing).

We'll confirm the deterministic seed policy — Priya will send the exact policy by EOD Mon (sanitized). Also: Ben, please share the temporary dashboard link when ready. We expect the Mon calibration to be representative; thanks for the clear deliverable list.

Jordan
Head of Platform Engineering
FinServe Labs
